Kelundra Smith’s superb 2024 play, The Wash, dramatizes the washerwomen’s strike of 1881, in which a handful of women meeting in a church basement grow into a citywide interracial movement that ultimately wins better labor conditions for all.

Smith’s writing sings under Tasia A. Jones’ excellent direction, supported by Lindsey McWhorter’s artful choreography, Janie E. Howland’s scenic design and Pamela Hersch’s projections of swaying trees, stained glass and more.
Kelundra Smith’s 2024 drama The Wash , which is based on a true story, revels spectacularly in the joy of strong Black women.
“The Wash” is a solid addition to that body of work: as an absorbing drama that draws a direct connection between racial injustice and economic struggle, with distinctively drawn characters...
The absolute joy of this production are the performances of its talented ensemble.

cn.t: Critics widely praise "The Wash" as a stirring, moving portrait of the 1881 Atlanta Washerwomen's Strike, with standout ensemble performances and timely resonance. A compelling, humorous, and triumphant production.
